Lyrics

Here are the lyrics from the site above:

verse:

Ilka ewe comes hame at even (x3)
Crookit hornie bides awa

chorus:

Ewie wi the crookit horn
May ye never see the morn
Ilka nicht you steal my corn
Ewie wi the crookit horn

Ilka ewie has a lambie (x3)
Crookit hornie she has twa

A the ewes gie milk eneuch (x3)
Crookit horn gies maist of a

Re: The Ewie Wi’ The Crookit Horn

O’Neill has two different settings in his Waifs and Strays of Gaelic Melody (#364 and 365). They are accompanied by a long note about their history, where he explains that the Ewie was a whisky-still with its crooked, or rather spiral apparatus. His reference is Wood’s Songs of Scotland, Edinburgh, 1848.

↳ Posted by brailsford on January 21st, 2024.

The Ewe Wi’ The Crookit Horn, X:6

I found this in G. Walker’s Collection of Favorite Dances no. 34, published in London some time around 1812--1820. The rhythm and slurs in the printed original are exactly as shown here, as are the 6 bars of part B. A crookit tune with a crookit name.

The B flat throughout is also as printed, though I actually prefer a B natural in part A, as in some of the other versions here.
